scope: Management of Behçet's syndrome in the 2025 EULAR update abstract stored in the app.

keyRecommendations.text: Colchicine is recommended first-line for mucocutaneous and joint involvement.
keyRecommendations.population: Behçet's syndrome with mucocutaneous or joint disease

keyRecommendations.text: Apremilast and immunosuppressives, including TNF inhibitors, are recommended for refractory patients.

Organ involvement is treated more aggressively with glucocorticoids and immunosuppressives for rapid remission, and early monoclonal TNF inhibitors are encouraged for organ- or life-threatening disease.

clinicalBottomLine: Individualise treatment for a relapsing disease: colchicine first for mucosa, skin, and joints; escalate refractory disease; use glucocorticoids plus immunosuppression, including early anti-TNF monoclonal antibodies, for organ-threatening disease.
notableCaveats: Pathergy testing and drug doses are not in this abstract and are not asked. The full recommendation table was not in the stored text.
